topic.title: When the reel flops, you get another reel
topic.claim: Influencer fees don't fall because brands can't measure what they buy, so a weak campaign gets fixed with more posts, not a lower price.
topic.behaviour: When a collaboration underperforms, creators add an extra post or extend the campaign. The fee stays where it was.
topic.mechanism: Nobody can say what a reel really sold, so nobody can argue for a refund. More output is the easiest way to look like you delivered.
topic.group: Creators, marketers and anyone who follows brand deals on Instagram
topic.moment: A creator you follow posts the fourth story about the same face cream in one week.

turn.believed: Brands pay creators for results and drop the ones who don't deliver.
turn.actually: Brands pay for activity they can't measure, and when it underperforms the fix is volume. The price survives because the result was never a number.

topic.feeling: watching a game where everyone knows the scoreboard is fake
topic.villain: a pay model where reach is sold but sales can't be traced
topic.because: Brands need to show their bosses a campaign ran. Creators need to protect their rate. More posts satisfy both and settle nothing.

proof.fact: In crowded categories like beauty and lifestyle, creators are adding extra posts or longer campaigns when a collaboration underperforms.

topic.payoff: The next time one product shows up in five stories, you're watching a make-good, not enthusiasm.
topic.send_to: The friend who thinks every creator loves the product they're promoting.
real_details: Brands are judging creators on engagement quality, audience relevance and campaign performance rather than follower counts.
topic.news_peg: Storyboard18 report on influencer fees and 'pricing rationalisation', 2026-11-20
topic.why_now: Brands are planning next year's budgets and creator rates are being reset.

score.why: The fourth story about the same face cream is a make-good, not enthusiasm. It fits his belief about influencer marketing and is an obvious one to send to a friend.
